In modern scholarship represented in the dossier, the text is cited primarily in connection with its narrative background; I. B. Horner refers to the story of Bhaddā Kuṇḍalakesā in the *Therīgāthā* commentary (on poem xlvi) in the context of courtesans who encountered the Buddhist teaching [Horner, Women under Primitive Buddhism].
Regarding textual reuse and parallels, DharmaNexus reports extensive Pali-internal reuse between the verses and the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, identifying six matching segments totaling 729 characters, with the longest match spanning segments 0.3–6.1 of the root text and segments 1634–1647 of the commentary [DharmaNexus]. Neither SuttaCentral nor DharmaNexus identifies any cross-language parallels or alignments in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan corpora [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
